skill.name: use-gemini-for-code-analysis
skill.description: Use Gemini CLI to analyze large codebases, map architecture, detect patterns, trace features, and return raw analysis results to the calling agent.
skill.summary: Runs Gemini CLI prompts for broad repository analysis and feature tracing.

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Gemini CLI wrapper that encourages broad repository scans and includes command examples. Several static hits are Markdown false positives, but the documented use still creates external-command and data exposure risk through --all-files, --yolo, and unfiltered output.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running Gemini with all files. Add guidance to exclude secrets and sensitive directories.
Remove --yolo from recommended use. Require normal CLI confirmations for commands that can read or modify files.
Add a review step that redacts secrets and labels Gemini output as unverified before sharing it.

semantic_findings.title: Repository Data Exposure to External Gemini CLI
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs Bash to run Gemini CLI with --all-files, which can send an entire repository to an external AI service. Private source code and secrets could leave the local environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly combine Bash execution, Gemini CLI, and --all-files examples. This clearly creates a third-party data exposure path for full repositories.

semantic_findings.title: Confirmation Bypass Encouraged
semantic_findings.description: The skill suggests --yolo to skip confirmations. This weakens safeguards around external CLI execution, broad file access, and third-party data transfer.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 25 directly recommends the confirmation-bypass flag. The parenthetical limit to non-destructive tasks reduces but does not remove the risk.

semantic_findings.title: Unfiltered Output Handling
semantic_findings.description: The skill says to return Gemini output directly and without modification. Sensitive file paths, snippets, or secrets found during analysis may be returned without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly requires complete raw output and no interpretation. This is a plausible leakage path if Gemini reports sensitive repository content.

content.user_title: Analyze Large Codebases with Gemini CLI
content.value_statement: Large repositories are difficult to map quickly with local context alone. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to call Gemini CLI for architecture, pattern, and implementation analysis.
actual_capabilities: Shows command patterns for running Gemini CLI with all repository files.
Supports architecture summaries across components, directories, and data flow.
Supports pattern detection requests across a repository.
Supports tracing feature implementation across files and integrations.
Supports prompts for performance, security, and code quality scans.
Returns Gemini CLI output without additional interpretation.
limitations: Requires Gemini CLI to be installed and authenticated in the execution environment.
May send repository contents to an external AI service when broad file access is used.
Does not validate or redact sensitive data before analysis.
Does not interpret Gemini output, so users must review the raw result.

use_cases.title: Map an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Create a high-level view of directories, components, entry points, and data flow before deeper work.

use_cases.title: Trace a feature implementation
use_cases.description: Find the files, integrations, and data paths behind a specific product capability.

use_cases.title: Review architecture and quality
use_cases.description: Ask Gemini to scan broad patterns, bottlenecks, security concerns, and design risks across a large codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Map the repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini CLI to map this repository. Return the main directories, components, data flow, and entry points.

prompt_templates.title: Find a pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini CLI to identify where this pattern appears: [pattern]. Include examples, related files, and likely risks.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini CLI to trace [feature]. Show the involved files, control flow, data flow, and external integrations.

prompt_templates.title: Assess architecture risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini CLI to review architecture risks. Focus on coupling, performance bottlenecks, security concerns, and maintainability tradeoffs.

output_examples.output: A concise report lists main modules, entry points, data flow, and design decisions from Gemini CLI results.
The response names related files, request flow, database interactions, and integration points for review.

output_examples.input: Scan for performance and security concerns.
output_examples.output: The output groups potential bottlenecks, risky patterns, and follow-up checks without modifying files.

best_practices: Confirm the repository scope and exclude secrets before using whole-codebase analysis.
Use focused prompts when the question targets one feature or module.
Review Gemini results before acting on recommendations or sharing them.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad scans on private repositories without permission.
Do not use confirmation-bypass flags for unclear or write-capable tasks.
Do not treat raw Gemini output as verified fact without local validation.

faq.question: Does this skill require Gemini CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Gemini CLI must be installed and authenticated before the skill can run its documented workflow.

faq.question: Does it modify code?
faq.answer: The documented workflow is analysis only. Command execution still needs care because the CLI can access project files.

faq.question: Can it analyze private repositories?
faq.answer: Only if you are allowed to share the files with Gemini. Exclude secrets and sensitive code first.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What analysis works best?
faq.answer: It fits architecture maps, pattern searches, feature tracing, and quality reviews across large repositories.

faq.question: Does it validate Gemini output?
faq.answer: No. It returns raw Gemini CLI results for the user or calling agent to review.
